original_test_intent: Reset the selected BMC NIC link-state control and verify that the intended physical interface returns to the specified operational link state and negotiated speed without leaving management connectivity degraded.
original_method: Select the unique row; map command argument `1` to an exact BMC NIC/port and management role; record pre-state from an independent console and interface/PHY source; issue the vendor-approved command once; timestamp any outage; after the specified settle window, read administrative/operational link state, speed/duplex and error counters using an approved command; verify management reachability and unrelated interfaces; retain logs and stop without retry on loss or mismatch.
manual_activity: An operator confirms command support, argument-to-port mapping, maintenance window and independent recovery; an agent may execute one approved reset and collect readback evidence through the safe path.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT firmware and vendor definition of `reset-nic-linkstate`
Exact meaning of argument `1` and physical/logical NIC, port and management-path mapping
Authoritative pre/post administrative and operational state, negotiated speed/duplex and settle timeout
Independent console or alternate management path, approval and recovery procedure
safety_requirements: Never reset an unknown NIC or the only available recovery path
Capture pre-state and confirm alternate console before the one-shot action
Bound outage/settle time and stop on wrong target, link flap, errors or unrecovered access
Do not repeat automatically; preserve console/network/BMC logs and restore through the independent path
agent_execution_scope: Collect redacted pre/post link, speed, duplex, counters and reachability
Run exactly one approved reset against the verified target
Correlate command result and outage/recovery timestamps with BMC/host logs
Do not guess argument mapping or expected speed, reset the only path, retry, reconfigure unrelated NICs or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve command semantics, NIC/port mapping and target firmware
Approve expected state/speed/duplex, observation command and timing
Approve maintenance window, independent recovery and final-state requirements
Review evidence and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `reset-nic-linkstate 1` is the stated stimulus, but neither the source nor DeepSeek identifies argument 1 or provides the required state/speed readback.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the vendor-supported reset once from an independent console, then query the named interface through an approved PHY/driver/BMC status command and confirm management recovery.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Argument 1, BMC-console context, link-status/link-speed title coverage, generic Criteria and 5/5-minute estimate remain; semantics and oracle are pending.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Establish a port-identity baseline, execute a single authorized reset, and compare timestamped physical/operational link and negotiated-speed evidence after bounded recovery.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds the omitted readback, exact port identity, expected values, alternate recovery and stop conditions.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Command success or restored SSH alone does not prove the intended NIC's physical link state or negotiated speed.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: The action can terminate its own transport; failover may make reachability appear healthy on a different NIC, so independent port-specific evidence is mandatory.

project_override_considerations: If argument `1` selects a shared/failover group rather than a physical port, the owner must define the expected active-path transition and port-specific oracle. If the command is unsupported on the build, record BLOCKED rather than substitute an unapproved network restart.
expected_evidence: BMC/SUT firmware plus command help/vendor semantics and argument-to-port map
Independent recovery readiness and approved maintenance window
Pre/post interface identity, administrative/operational state, speed/duplex and error counters
Single command output/exit status with monotonic outage, settle and recovery timestamps
BMC/network/host logs, unrelated-interface invariance, final management reachability and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items require link status and link speed after reset, but Procedure only issues the reset and Criteria says merely that data is readable/correct. No readback command, interface identity, expected status/speed or timing is provided, so the stated coverage cannot be judged from the source steps.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The reset-and-readback intent is clear and conditionally executable once the vendor mapping, oracle and independent recovery are supplied; those pending inputs do not invalidate static review.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Functionality row 2255 Wistron-BMC Sanity-00037-V001: approve BMC firmware and exact `reset-nic-linkstate` semantics; map argument `1` to the physical/logical NIC, port and management/failover role; provide the approved state/speed/duplex readback and expected pre/post values, settle/outage timeout and counter tolerances; approve one-shot maintenance authorization, independent console/recovery and final state, and decide how to restore the missing readback step while preserving Master.

review_improvement: Preserves the named reset stimulus while restoring the title's omitted link-status and speed verification and preventing alternate-path reachability from masking a failed target port.
independent_technical_reasoning: A NIC link-state reset is transport-destructive when invoked through the same BMC network being tested. Exit status cannot be relied on if the session drops, and post-action reachability may arrive through bonding/failover rather than the intended port. Therefore the case needs an independently observed port identity, physical/operational state, negotiated rate and bounded recovery timeline; without those, `readable and correct` is not an engineering oracle.
